title: Clickstream: Kinesis vs Kafka
brief: An API publishes 5k click events/s into a stream with 12 partitions (shards); 12 loaders (500 events/s each) write them to the warehouse. Side A uses Kafka (3 MSK brokers), side B Kinesis. Decide which you'd run at today's traffic and at 4x.

scenarios.label: Burst x3 for 10 s
scenarios.about: A campaign triples traffic to 15k/s for 10 s. A Kinesis shard takes 1,000 records/s; what happens to the rest?
scenarios.watch: At 10 s traffic triples for 10 s. Watch the Kinesis block turn red and the errors number climb: its shards reject what they can't take. Kafka queues the extra and drains it afterwards.

scenarios.label: 20k/s, re-sharded
scenarios.about: Traffic is 20k/s. Both sides get 24 partitions, 24 faster loaders and more API replicas up front. Which is cheaper now?
scenarios.watch: Nothing breaks after the re-sharding at 0 s. Read the cost row: per-shard and per-PUT pricing at 20k/s.

scenarios.label: Steady 5k events/s
scenarios.about: Both keep up. Kinesis bills per shard-hour and per PUT; Kafka per broker-hour.
scenarios.watch: Nothing breaks, so both canvases look the same. Read the cost row in the table.

questions: Why is Kinesis cheaper at 5k/s but not at 20k/s? Where is the crossover?
In the burst, Kinesis has the smaller backlog. Why is that not good news?
How would you make Kinesis survive the burst: more shards, on-demand mode, or retrying producers? What does each cost?
Kafka on MSK still needs broker sizing, upgrades and partition rebalancing. How much is that worth to you per month?
hints: In the burst, look at errors next to the backlog rows.
12 shards accept 12k records/s; the other 3k/s are rejected. Kafka takes them all and lets the backlog grow.

Kinesis: $0.015 per shard-hour plus $0.014 per million PUTs, so cost grows with traffic; Kafka's 3 brokers cost $0.63/hr flat until they fill up. Kinesis rejects writes above shards x 1,000/s, so size shards for the peak (or use on-demand mode) and retry on the producer.
_notes: Graph: client -> api (25 x 1k) -> events (12 partitions) -> loader (12 x 500/s = 6k/s drain, $0.10 each). Kafka: 12 x 10k/s per partition (estimate), $0.63/hr flat. Kinesis: 1,000 records/s per shard (AWS limit), $0.015/shard-hr + $0.014 per million PUTs. Steady 5k: Kinesis $0.43 vs Kafka $0.63 for the stream (sim totals $4.13 vs $4.33). Burst x3 (15k for 10 s): Kinesis rejects above 12k/s (3.3% errors over the run, p99 49 ms), backlog peaks 60k; Kafka takes all 15k, backlog peaks 90k and drains at 1k/s (50k left at 60 s). Scale (20k, 24 shards/partitions, 24 x 1k loaders, api 40): Kinesis $1.37 vs Kafka $0.63 (totals $7.77 vs $7.03). Crossover with shards sized to traffic: Kinesis costs ~$0.065/hr per 1k events/s, so ~9.6k/s matches Kafka's $0.63. Not modeled: on-demand Kinesis, producer retries, Kafka broker limits beyond partitions. Checked in frontend/src/lessons/content.test.ts.
